name: VidVerge
description: VidVerge brings two focused video workflows together: create polished product videos or enhance footage you already have.

apps.name: Video Engine
apps.description: The autonomous video and motion graphics engine — two pipelines that each turn a single input into a finished, broadcast-ready MP4 with no manual editing. SaaS Motion Reel reads a product URL with the Apify scraper for real brand colours, logo and copy, writes and voices the script with ElevenLabs, times every word with Deepgram nova-3, then has Claude Opus 5 engineer a Remotion composition (3-Object Rule, spring physics, lexical subtitles locked to the word timings) and renders it. Vox Documentary takes a topic, writes fifteen sequential four-second beats with GPT-5.6, narrates them, builds a torn-paper editorial collage still for every beat, animates each one as rigid stop-motion with Seedance 2.0 Fast, and assembles the film through the DocumentaryMaster composition with five-frame cross-dissolves and the ambient bed ducked to -22 dB under the narration. Every run is tracked live through QUEUED, INGESTING, AUDIO_SYNTHESIS, GENERATING_VISUALS, AUDITING and RENDERING against the vge_video_jobs table, so a reloaded tab picks the job back up, and finished masters play and download in the app.

apps.name: Vidverge Agent
apps.description: The primary agent hub for Vidverge — a premium, near-black single screen whose identity is a living light wave. A multi-trail SVG motion wave (pure CSS keyframes, no video or animation library) dips into a smooth V across the full width with a bright particle travelling along the main path, and it reacts to what the agent is doing: calm breathing when idle, a faster brighter particle with shimmering trails while working, a one-shot sweep that illuminates the whole path on completion, and a gentle amber trail when something needs attention. A floating VIDVERGE label over the wave shows the live state (Ready to create / Thinking... / Generating / Editing / Finalizing). Below it sits the frosted pill Create bar: attachment button, a full-width 'What do you want to create?' input, a dropdown that routes the brief to any of the six studios (SceneForge, Faceless Content, Script-to-Video, SaaS Verger, Video Enhancer, Ads Studio) and a golden Create button — submitting opens the selected studio with the brief prefilled. Underneath, a compact Recent Jobs queue shows up to five projects with stage label, thin golden progress bar and a preview tile, beside a small Activity panel with an equaliser heartbeat and the agent's last few actions. The Create bar now uploads any attachment once, hands the brief and durable file URL to the selected studio's create screen, and opens that studio immediately. Recent Jobs polls the studios' persisted WorkspaceDB projects, reflects real in-flight state in the wave and status label, and opens the owning studio project when a row is clicked.

apps.name: Faceless
apps.description: A standalone faceless-video pipeline built as an AI EDITOR that happens to generate footage, not an AI video generator. Opus 5 is the editorial director; audio drives the edit, so every visual change is justified by what the narrator is saying at that exact second. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: narration is recorded FIRST through the platform ElevenLabs voiceover endpoint and immediately read back through Deepgram nova-3 for real word-level timestamps, because analyzeScript needs timing that raw text cannot give. From there the run is createFacelessFilm -> generateNarration -> analyzeScript (hook/body/resolution, FacelessMode, a music arc that must actually move) -> buildAssetIndex (the workspace's own rendered films, saved videos and generations, read by the faceless-assets function) -> createEditorialTimeline -> createVisualPlan -> selectAssets/generateAssets -> prepareAssets -> createMotionPlan -> compileFilmSpec -> validateFilmSpec -> renderFilm -> runMechanicalQA -> runCreativeQA -> finalizeFilm. createEditorialTimeline calls Opus 5 with the verbatim FacelessEditorialDirector system prompt (apps/Faceless/lib/editorialDirectorPrompt.ts) in two shapes, because the Claude proxy caps output at 8,192 tokens and Opus cannot disable thinking: one SPINE call that fixes continuity, the asset mix and where every cut falls against the narration, then WINDOW calls that fully populate six beats at a time with the continuity guide and everything already directed in view, so the novelty rule and match cuts hold across a window boundary. The grammar is enforced in code rather than hoped for: camera moves are clamped to the six defined types and their exact scale ranges, a text overlay whose words are already in the narration is DROPPED as a caption, the hook beat is forced to statement_punch or reveal_pullback with text inside 1500ms, and any run of more than four identical visualTypes is broken by mode. createVisualPlan is the last stop before money is spent: it scores novelty across every rolling five-beat window and forces a visual deviation below 0.3, enforces the cost hierarchy (Tier 2 searches real Pexels stock clips through the secure faceless-assets BYOK proxy, then falls back to Unsplash stills when Pexels is unavailable; tier 5 AI video ~$0.40 against ~$0.05 for a generated still, never more than 40% of beats, a 60s film budgeted under $4.00, lowest-impact beats downgraded to tier 4 with their prompts rewritten as a single decisive frame), and resolves the match-cut DAG into ordered waves so dependent pairs generate SEQUENTIALLY while independent beats run in parallel. prepareAssets is asset-type-aware rather than trim-to-duration: a long clip gets its most relevant subrange, a generated still is marked for parallax, a sub-2s clip is not padded. The FilmSpec is deep-frozen; a revision compiles v(n+1) and never mutates in place. QA is TWO separate stages with different failure paths: mechanical QA measures the actual rendered file in the browser (duration within 0.1s, decoded audio track present and in sync with the first word timestamp, no black run over 0.5s by canvas luma sampling, frame cadence via requestVideoFrameCallback, no silence over 1.2s inside the spoken section) and on failure gets ONE deterministic repair and ONE re-render before aborting, never an escalation to a model; creative QA is Opus Vision on real frames from the finished render, and a fail produces a TARGETED reviseFilm that patches only the named beats, capped at two passes before the film ships as it stands. Rendering goes through a RenderAdapter abstraction (apps/Faceless/lib/renderAdapter.ts) with HyperFramesAdapter as the only implementation Faceless uses; it emits a new self-contained HyperFrames composition (camera grammar, five transition types, six text treatments, parallax stills, looped short clips, arc-driven music ducking, a branded motion card instead of a black frame for any unresolved beat) to the live platform render service at 1920x1080/30fps through the faceless-render function. No code is shared with Track B, ProductLaunch or SceneForge, and the HeyGen avatar API is never called. UI is three screens: brief (topic, script, mode grammar) -> a pipeline view that shows every beat's visual type, camera, tier, match cuts, cost downgrades and novelty deviations as they are decided -> the finished MP4 with its tier mix, spend, spec version and any open editorial notes. WorkspaceDB checkpoints every run and lets the running screen resume a recent unfinished film; generated stills and clips are indexed for reuse by later films, avoiding repeat generation cost.

apps.name: Vergeye
apps.description: Vergeye is the competitive positioning studio: a customer enters THEIR OWN website address and comes out with a researched comparison against auto-discovered competitors and a finished positioning video. Four screens, one analysis object that each screen adds a layer to. (1) YOUR BRAND — one URL in a hero input; the vergeye-ops server function fetches the home page and the /pricing page, reads the linked stylesheets for the site's real colour palette, and gpt-5.6-terra extracts product name, tagline, category, audience, pricing, USP, positioning and features into an EDITABLE brand summary card. The extracted brand colour becomes the app's accent and brands the generated video; when a site paints in a colour space the reader cannot resolve, nothing is claimed and a colour picker is offered instead. (2) COMPETITORS — discovery runs by itself: three Google searches ('<name> alternatives 2026', 'best <category> compared', '<name> vs competitors') through /api/search, then the model names 6-8 real competing PRODUCTS with their own official domains, rejecting review sites, listicles, directories, app stores and social profiles. Each competitor's site is then read ONE AT A TIME (sequential on purpose — eight parallel page-plus-model reads is how a run gets itself rate-limited) into the same profile shape. Grid cards carry the site's own favicon or a monogram tile, an Include/Exclude toggle, and a plain statement when a site blocks automated readers, with Retry; competitors can also be added by hand. (3) COMPARE — a seven-row side-by-side table (Pricing, Key features, Target audience, USP, Strengths, Weaknesses, Positioning) with every cell filled by gpt-5.6-sol from the pages already read, the customer's own column highlighted in their accent, and ANY CELL click-to-edit. Export PNG snapshots exactly what is on screen through html2canvas (cells are divs, not inputs, and every colour in the captured subtree is a literal rgba so the capture is not grey). A right sidebar carries four AI-written sections: what competitors do better, your unique advantages, positioning gaps, messaging improvements. (4) VIDEO — a 30-45 second script and its 4-6 scene shot list are written from the advantages and the gaps, every line and every camera prompt editable, with optional character-photo and product-mockup uploads used as the opening frame. Veo films it through /api/veo/generate-long-video (8s per clip, each chained off the previous clip's last frame, auto-stitched; Veo 3.1 Fast or full Veo 3.1), then Remotion post-processes the finished cut at 1920x1080 with brand lower thirds, the three differentiator bands, one stat drawn from the comparison and a closing CTA card — the video model is explicitly told to draw NO text so the graphics stay exact and re-renderable. Download video, and 'Use in Ads Studio' records the hand-off on the saved row and opens Ads Studio with the script already in step 1. PERSISTENCE: every change writes the whole analysis to the vergeye_comparisons table a second later under an auto-generated name ('Pictory vs 6 competitors'), so the Saved Comparisons tab is a real per-visitor history — reopening one restores the edited cells, the insights, the script and any render still in flight, which 'Resume render' then adopts rather than paying for twice. The table is serverHooksOnly and scoped by owner_key; every page read, search, model call and render goes through vergeye-ops, because a competitor's site sends no CORS headers and the published bundle's workspace token is public.

apps.name: Video Enhancer
apps.description: The all-in-one AI video editor, now focused entirely on one professional STUDIO workspace — Product Video is no longer embedded here. The editor is agentic from the first second: drop footage in and, before the creator touches a control, it transcribes the audio with word-level timing (Deepgram word timestamps, Whisper as the fallback with words aligned to the measured speech envelope), measures every silence and filler word, samples frames to locate the subject and the near-static stretches, and produces a CUT PLAN — reviewable cards, each with a type (trim / remove filler / cut silence / captions / B-roll / effect / text / transition / reframe), an exact timecode, a thumbnail, the reason it helps, a predicted % watch-time retention (the model's read of the content blended with the local signal estimate), and Accept / Reject. Accepting applies the edit to the timeline; Accept all applies them cuts-first so captions never describe footage that is gone. A chat panel takes plain-English requests mid-edit ('make this punchy', 'remove all silences', 'where am I losing viewers?') and answers with more cards and whole-video actions. TRANSCRIPT-FIRST EDITING: every word is time-linked — click to seek, strike a word or a whole sentence and that segment is cut from the video, one tap clears every um / uh / like / you know / basically / actually, and a cut can be restored (the range is spliced back into the neighbouring clip, so splits, reorders and inserted B-roll survive). AUTO-REFRAME to 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 keeps the subject centred using the browser's native FaceDetector where it exists and a skin-tone + edge-energy saliency pass where it does not, with a smoothed keyframe path, a side-by-side original-vs-output proof, a confidence read-out, and manual / centre overrides; several formats export in one run. B-ROLL SLOTS: silences, long pauses and low-motion stretches are flagged on their own green track; each slot can be generated from a prompt written off the surrounding transcript, replaced with the creator's own clip, or filled from the workspace clip library. PROFESSIONAL TIMELINE: colour-coded tracks (grey raw, blue cut, green B-roll, amber overlay + text, yellow captions, orange FX), a retention heat strip over the ruler, trim handles on every edge, split at playhead, drag-to-reorder, Shift-click multi-select for batch edits, zoom, and per-clip crop (aspect lock or freeform, 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 presets), brightness, contrast, saturation, speed 0.25×–4×, reverse and opacity. OVERLAYS: the workspace logo or any image, dragged and resized on the stage, with opacity, rotation, always-on or in/out timing, SVG MASKING (rectangle, ellipse or freehand polygon with feather and invert), BLEND MODES (Normal / Screen / Multiply / Overlay / Soft Light) and AUTO-TRACKING by block matching — an optical-flow approximation that makes the overlay follow a subject and reports a real confidence score. CAPTIONS: fourteen animated presets (Minimal, Bold, Gradient, Karaoke, TikTok Pop, Neon Glow, Cinematic, Handwritten, Creator Punch, Newsroom, Comic Burst, Luxury Gold, Gaming HUD, Desi Bold) plus font, size, colour, active-word colour, outline, shadow, position and a vertical nudge, burned in or downloaded as SRT. TEXT LAYERS: animated entrances (Typewriter, Fade In, Slide Up/Down/Left/Right, Scale Pop, Glitch) and exits (Fade Out, Slide Out, Scale Down) with full type control. EFFECTS and grades (Lens Flare, Light Leak, Vignette, Bloom, Flash, Film Grain; Cinematic / Warm / Cool / B&W / Vintage) per clip or globally, and TRANSITIONS on any cut point (Crossfade, Whip Pan, Flash Cut, Dip to Black, Glitch Cut, Zoom Punch, Spin) at 0.1–2s, rendered as real overlapping sequences. Keyboard: S split, Space play/pause, Cmd+Z undo, Delete remove selection, arrows nudge. The edit autosaves to ve_studio_projects every 30 seconds with a backing-off retry. EXPORT is MP4 / H.264 / 30fps at 1080p through veh-render, which compiles the same descriptors the preview used, so the render matches the stage: 16:9 lands at a true 1920×1080 and 9:16 at a true 1080×1920 (the 1920×1080 master is cover-cropped up by the platform's portrait re-encode), while 1:1 and 4:5 are delivered centred inside a 1920×1080 file because the render service is pinned to that canvas — which is also why 720p and 4K are shown as unavailable rather than promised. Upload by drag-and-drop or picker up to 500MB. Still the handoff target for SceneForge and the Vidverge Agent: a video sent here loads as the first clip and the whole analysis pass runs on it automatically.

apps.name: Script-to-Video
apps.description: The rebuilt script-to-film pipeline with Claude Opus 5 as the single director brain: paste a script (never rewritten) and Opus breaks it into independent scenes, deciding per scene how it gets made — cinematic live-action shots on Veo (with a hard rule against on-screen text), deterministic motion graphics rendered in the browser with HTML/SVG + GSAP (eleven varied treatments — kinetic type, documentary lower-thirds, flowcharts, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, timelines, comparisons, node maps, quotes, annotated images — each with its own content-matched palette, never a repeated generic card), real product screenshots inside animated phone/laptop/browser mockups (Veo is never asked to recreate a UI), and reused project assets with cinematic motion and exact labels. Continuity is frame-chained: after each Veo scene the last frame is extracted and Opus reads its visual attributes (lighting, character, environment, camera) into the next scene's prompt, so consecutive cinematic shots carry the same person, place and light; independent scenes render in parallel. After every render Opus checks the clip against its script segment and flags mismatches. Every scene is independent — own spec, status, cached clip — so regenerating one scene never touches the rest, and a docked Director bar revises any single scene from a plain-English note. Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser: normalization, audio handling and the final MP4 cut, no server renderer. On the Final screen, an opt-in Finish step can add ElevenLabs narration from the untouched original script, an ElevenLabs music bed automatically ducked beneath narration and native scene sound, and scene-timed burned-in captions built from each stored script segment and measured duration; generated tracks and settings are persisted and reused. Runs persist to the database at every step and resume after reloads. Legacy projects stay watchable in the Library.

apps.name: SceneForge
apps.description: SceneForge has four faces and opens on the fast one. DIRECTOR turns an explanatory script on ANY subject into a film: a visual-director model cuts the narration into timed segments and decides what graphic explains each line (dramatic text reveal, timeline, chart, flow with travelling particles, diagram, orbit, map, Ken Burns photograph, callout, keyword highlight), Remotion draws those graphics from code with interpolate() and spring(), and the HeyGen narrator - a HeyGen voice, or the customer's own recording lip-synced to the presenter - is composited as a circular picture-in-picture over them into one 1920x1080 MP4 with a frosted caption bar and 0.3s dissolves; the plan is re-timed to the narration's real measured length so graphics land on the words, and every scene is editable against a live looping preview before anything is rendered. AVATAR STUDIO (default) is a one-screen HeyGen video creator: the live HeyGen avatar library is paged in as a card grid with an Indian avatars tab first (HeyGen tags no ethnicity, so the tab matches each look's own name, language, accent and tags, and a flag button on any card pins it there) and an All tab with search; the live HeyGen voice catalog loads as a searchable dropdown with Indian voices first and an Indian-English voice pre-selected when the account has one (v2/voices supplies the labels, v3/voices supplies the verdict on which voices a v3 render will accept); a 1,500-character script box with a live count and an Improve script button that polishes the copy through the workspace gpt-5.6-terra proxy; and settings for aspect ratio (Portrait 9:16 default, Landscape 16:9), resolution (1080p/720p), background (colour swatch, public image URL, or the avatar's own backdrop) and speaking speed 0.8x-1.5x. Generate resolves the look's engine off supported_api_engines (avatar_iv, then avatar_v, then avatar_iii), submits POST /v3/videos with fit cover, polls every eight seconds behind an eased progress bar, reattaches to an in-flight render after a page reload, and finishes as an inline MP4 player with a Download MP4 button; the last five renders stay in a Recent panel with poster, script and one-tap download, and a missing HeyGen key surfaces as a plain Connect your HeyGen API key in Settings message. Nothing in it is mocked - every avatar, voice and video comes from the account's live HeyGen API through the workspace proxy. FULL PIPELINE, one click away in the header and unchanged: SceneForge v4 is a talking-head + documentary motion-graphics studio: the HeyGen avatar master carries the film (intro, transitions and CTA on camera) while MIDDLE VISUAL SECTIONS cut in over its picture and the presenter's narration keeps playing underneath, documentary style. The single orchestrator LLM writes the script, then produces a full video blueprint: every middle scene gets a customer-switchable type — AI VIDEO (real generated footage on Gemini Omni Flash; an unchanged prompt reuses its clip), MOTION GRAPHIC (the new GSAP + SVG engine: branching diagrams, flowcharts, timelines, comparisons, list reveals, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, node graphs, annotated images and text reveals, all rendered from a structured spec whose every string and number appears EXACTLY as written — important text never goes inside AI video; scenes preview live in the browser and are captured with MediaRecorder into real video clips), IMAGE (one strong Omni Flash still), or TEXT OVERLAY (a deterministic animated headline captured the same way). The blueprint timeline is colour-coded: HeyGen blue, AI video amber, motion graphics green, images orange, text teal. Scenes are independently editable — switching a type or editing a spec regenerates ONLY that scene, every clip is cached, re-assembly never re-renders finished scenes, and the HeyGen master stays locked unless explicitly re-recorded. Final assembly composites the middle clips over the continuous avatar master: 9:16 films run through the platform's server-side FFmpeg overlay compositor (base narration audio kept uninterrupted), 16:9 films use one deterministic compositing render because the platform's FFmpeg compositor is portrait-only today. Steps: topic → deep-research script → live HeyGen v3 avatar render (resumable after reload) → style → the STUDIO WORKBENCH, one screen that replaced the old stack of step boards: a top bar with a live provider selector (each engine marked ready or not set up, with the reason), Generate All and Export; a large centre preview of the finished film or the selected scene; a scrollable bottom timeline of scene cards carrying a real thumbnail, scene number, duration and status icon, with a right-click menu for regenerate / edit script / replace with upload / switch type / skip / delete; and one collapsible right panel holding Script, Character, Style, Music, Scene Context and B-roll. Generation reports real per-scene progress with a time and credit estimate, and any failure names the provider and its status instead of spinning. Gemini Vision reads each generated first frame for scene context, auto lower-third copy, a colour palette and B-roll search terms. B-roll rides as a MUTED corner picture-in-picture between a chosen start and end time, so the original audio is never interrupted. Export renders the whole film in ONE server-side Remotion pass that draws the title card, lower thirds, transitions, B-roll and closing CTA over the clips frame-accurately, with narration, music bed and any uploaded audio intact, then downloads as MP4. Underneath it the same engine runs: parallel middle-visual production with per-scene Retry / switch type / Skip → audio-preserving assembly, six quality checks, inline player, ElevenLabs music bed under a 16:9 master → editor handoff — plus the built-in Asset Studio (Omni Flash stills attached straight onto scenes, always reused, never re-billed) and natural-language script/scene/style/assembly changes via Verger.

apps.name: Ads Studio
apps.description: Agentic short-form ad engine: product URL + avatar + assets in, a finished professional ad out. A linear 8-step workflow (Product → Research → Angles → Script → Scene Plan → Generate → Review → Variations) with Claude Opus 5 as the single creative brain. Research crawls the product site (plus /reviews, /testimonials, /pricing and /about) and extracts a structured direct-response brief — features, pricing, pain points, desires, objections, mechanism, awareness level and real customer language, each marked [VERIFIED] or [INFERRED], never invented — that the user can correct inline. Opus then generates 8–12 genuinely different ad angles (selectable cards with an 'Opus picks best' judge), writes a 4–7 clip script (Hook → Problem → Agitate → Solution → Proof → Benefit → single CTA) under hard per-duration word limits (4s→9, 6s→13, 8s→17, 10s→22 words) with live word-count validation and per-clip duration selectors, and directs a full per-clip scene plan — camera, framing, micro-action, gesture, expression, environment, lighting, ONE locked voice description reused verbatim across all clips, continuity notes, overlay plan and an assembled production Veo prompt (clip 1 must open on a first-second pattern interrupt, never a static talking head). Generation is an agentic loop: each clip renders on the platform video model with the uploaded avatar as the character reference, Opus vision inspects the take against the plan (action, framing, flow, same character, clutter, composition), a rejected take auto-regenerates ONCE with the inspector's adjusted prompt (max 2 attempts), and the final frame of each clip is read by Opus into the next clip's continuity clause. Real screenshots are never recreated by the video model — they composite AFTER generation inside GSAP-animated phone/laptop/browser/tablet/monitor mockups, alongside kinetic text callouts, review cards, animated stat counters, CTA buttons, arrow highlights, a logo watermark and styled burned-in captions of each spoken line (all GSAP + SVG rendered to canvas, no Remotion). Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser — chroma-keyed overlay compositing, normalization, concat, faststart MP4 — with a progress bar, a collapsible FFmpeg debug log and a download button. A Variations step has Opus write alternative hooks, bodies and CTAs (up to 3×2×2 = 12 combinations); building a variation reuses every clip whose line is unchanged and regenerates only the clips whose spoken line differs, then re-assembles, each with its own download. The session persists to localStorage, so a refresh resumes mid-run. A RECIPES section in the left rail (below the eight steps) is the app's fourth top-level surface, with TWO sub-sections on an inner tab strip. SAVED VIDEOS is the workspace clip library read through the vv-workspace-videos server function, filterable by the engine that made it (Runway / Veo / Omni Flash / Assembled / Everything), each card showing a poster frame, the generation date and time, Download and 'Use in Ad' (attaches the clip as product footage on Step 1). RUNWAY RECIPES holds the Runway-powered recipe templates — Product Ads, UGC, Product Swaps, Multi-Shot films, Localized Ads, Campaign Imagery and Stock Images — plus raw text/image-to-video on the Runway Gen 4 models (Gen 4.5 and Gen 4 Turbo); every generation is quoted before anything is charged, and this is still the ONE place Runway recipes live. The Product Ad and UGC recipes now CAST AND POSITION THEMSELVES: upload the product image and write what the product is (name + description), and gpt-5.6-terra automatically writes the UGC presenter (name, appearance, personality) and the ad angle (the pain it speaks to, one spoken hook and a CTA) into an 'Auto-generated' card directly under the product inputs — each half regenerable on its own — and both are folded into the recipe's own creative brief, so the clip is filmed with that presenter and that angle. The former CHARACTER STUDIO and AUTO-WRITE ANGLE sub-tabs were REMOVED in that change: their two jobs now happen by themselves inside the recipe flow, so never point anyone at them. Opening Recipes parks the eight-step workflow exactly where it stands; nothing in the session changes until 'Use in Ad' is pressed on a saved clip. Standalone — shares nothing with Product Video, SceneForge, Video Enhancer or Script-to-Video.

apps.name: Faceless Content
apps.description: Topic in, one finished faceless MP4 out — no templates, everything written and filmed from scratch on every run. The Create tab is a single clean form: a topic (with a 'Suggest a topic' button), a niche pill picker (Explainer / Documentary / Crime), a target length (2 / 5 / 8 minutes, default 5), an orientation toggle (16:9 landscape or 9:16 portrait) and a video-model toggle (Veo 3 or Runway Turbo), under one full-width electric-blue Generate. Pressing Generate replaces the form with a terminal-style progress log whose lines fade in as the pipeline advances, driven by a 2-second poll of the project row so a reload resumes mid-run. The pipeline: Claude Opus 5 acts as the Faceless Script Writer — it verifies its own facts, writes the body first and the three-layer hook afterwards (cold drop, stakes sentence, peak teases), and follows the blueprint for the chosen niche (Crime: Normal Day → Discovery → investigation loops → the Turn at 70% → Resolution → gut-punch closer; Explainer: short hook → 5–12 escalating segments → held-back closer; Documentary: the Surface → descent loops → a named human core → the Why in numbers → a return to the opening image), returning three title options, a thumbnail line, timecoded VO/VISUAL blocks and a fact-check list. A second Opus 5 call turns every VISUAL line into a camera-only shot prompt — physical verbs, FOV in degrees, white balance in Kelvin, a cut every ~2 seconds, positive-only phrasing and a verbatim 'NO MUSIC. SFX ONLY' audio lock. Scenes then render SEQUENTIALLY so each one can seed from the previous scene's last frame (extracted server-side with ffmpeg) for visual continuity, on Veo 3 or, when the founder's RUNWAY_API_KEY is configured, Runway Gen-4 Turbo through the secrets proxy — a missing key falls back to Veo 3 with a toast rather than failing. Finished clips are concatenated server-side into one MP4. The Result screen is a full-width player with Download, the three title options, a collapsed script accordion with timecodes, the fact-check list, and Regenerate / New Video. The History tab is a two-column grid of past videos (thumbnail, topic, niche badge, date, duration, Download). Dark #0A0A0A UI with #1A1A1A cards, electric-blue #3B82F6 accent, Inter for the UI and JetBrains Mono for the terminal and script view. Projects and scenes persist to the fc_projects and fc_scenes tables.

apps.name: Product Launch
apps.description: Vidverge's launch-film app, REBUILT 6 Oct 2026 as an AUTONOMOUS FILM-AGENT PIPELINE. The mental model is one sentence: Opus decides the film, ProductLaunch executes it reliably. The whole four-screen engine of 4 Oct is gone — no brief, no five fields, no tone picker, no single fixed composition, no lib/filmSource.ts template. There is ONE input, a product URL, and ten measured steps: (1) EXTRACTION — ps-brand-scrape reads the homepage plus up to three discovered pages (/features, /product, /how-it-works, /pricing) server-side and photographs each; THIS APP assigns every asset handle and source_url from what actually came back, then claude-opus-5 turns the harvest into a ProductContext (product understanding, brand extraction, ranked assets with a film_usability directive each, ui_richness, extraction_confidence, extraction_gaps and manufacture_required). The model never invents a URL because it never produces one; an asset it described that was not captured is dropped and one it ignored is appended. (2) CONCEPTS — Opus writes 2-3 genuinely competing FilmSpec drafts (narrative_arc in plain language, 5-8 scenes with visual_treatment, SDK components, asset handles, narration beat and motion_intensity, typography system, 450-900 frames) and scores each itself. Text only: concepts are cheap and renders are not. (3) SELECTION — highest concept_score wins, ties broken by asset coverage; ConceptSelector shows all of them with an asset-coverage audit and auto-selects after 5s unless the creator overrules it. (4) COMPONENT PLAN — Opus translates the chosen FilmSpec into a ComponentPlan of exact typed component instances with concrete props, absolute start frames and back-to-front layers, with a 2-attempt repair loop against the validator; frames are then rebalanced arithmetically so the timeline is true rather than asserted. (5) CODEGEN — Opus writes Film.tsx against the plan and the SDK types; it never sees the FilmSpec, so it cannot reinterpret the creative. (6) COMPILE GATE — deterministic, free, and upstream of every render: a TSX scanner (strings, templates, comments, JSX tags, bracket balance, generics told apart from tags) plus the SDK prop schema prove every component exists, every prop type and union literal is valid, every resolveAsset handle is in the registry, no import reaches outside the allowlist, no runtime global is redeclared and every scene Sequence matches the plan. Failures go back to claude-sonnet-5 with their own errors, up to 3 attempts, and a repair that makes things worse is discarded. If it still cannot pass, the film is PRINTED deterministically from the already-validated plan rather than rendered broken. (7) RENDER — buildFilmBundle concatenates the SDK runtime source, the inlined asset registry and the generated film into ONE module (the render service takes a single compositionTsx importing only react and remotion), submitted to /api/render/remotion at the pinned 1920x1080 / 30fps. (8) TECHNICAL QA — 24 frames pulled via /api/video/frames and stitched into one 6x4 contact sheet on a canvas, with real pixel-variance blank-frame detection and edge-bleed detection handed on as hints. (9) CRITIC — one claude-opus-5 vision call receives the sheet WITH the FilmSpec it was meant to execute and the ProductContext it came from, so it can tell an execution failure from a concept that was never achievable given manufacture_required; returns CriticOutput (overall_score, shippable, scene_assessments, film_level_issues with fix_instructions, single_biggest_problem, director_note). (10) ITERATION — lib/iteration-manager decides: stop if shippable, if the critic says stop, if improvement_delta is under 0.08, or if the score is over 0.75 with nothing critical; otherwise reviseFilmSpec applies ONLY the named fixes and the film re-renders, to a ceiling of 3 iterations. The BEST-scoring cut wins, not the last. Files: App.tsx, types/{product-context,film-spec,component-plan,critic}.types.ts, sdk/{component-sdk.types,component-schema,validate-props,runtime-source}.ts + sdk/components/index.tsx, prompts/{extraction,concept-generation,component-plan,code-generation,critic}.prompt.ts, pipeline/{extract,concepts,select-concept,component-plan,codegen,compile-check,render,qa,critic,revise}.ts, lib/{ai-client,asset-registry,iteration-manager,pipeline-events,platform,tsx-scan}.ts, components/{LaunchUi,PipelineProgress,ConceptSelector,FilmSpecViewer,CriticReport,VideoResult}.tsx. SDK: 24 primitives in five families (UI BrowserFrame/Dashboard/Cursor/Highlight/Tooltip, Typography MassiveType/KineticText/WordReveal/SplitText/TypeOn, Motion Parallax/Camera/Zoom/BlurMask/Morph/Particle, Composition SplitScreen/FloatingUI/Perspective/Grid/FullBleed, Media Screenshot/Logo/MetricCounter) with RENDER_CONSTRAINTS the model never chooses. Models: claude-opus-5 for extraction, concepts, plan, codegen and critique; claude-sonnet-5 for the compile-fix loop only; both over /proxy/anthropic/v1/messages with X-Workspace-DB-Token. Still ZERO content — no sample product, no demo concept, no placeholder film; a URL that cannot be read stops the run instead of inventing one. No WorkspaceDB persistence: a run lives in screen state.

apps.name: Voice Studio
apps.description: Full-stack AI voice and avatar creation — seven standalone modules behind one dark, amber-accented tab rail (sidebar on desktop, a scrolling strip on mobile). TEXT TO SPEECH: a large script box that handles English, Devanagari Hindi and romanised Hinglish, a searchable voice dropdown where Indian voices are badged 🇮🇳 and sorted first (matched on each voice's own accent and description labels and its name, never guessed from a premade American voice, with a flag button on any row to add or remove the badge by hand) and every voice auditionable from its real ElevenLabs sample before a credit is spent, stability / similarity / style sliders plus a speaker-boost toggle, a model picker (Multilingual v2 default, Turbo v2.5, Flash v2.5) and an output-format picker (MP3 128 default, MP3 192, PCM 44.1kHz and PCM 24kHz, each PCM option wrapped in a WAV header so it plays and downloads) — then an in-browser waveform player with Download. VOICE CLONE: drag in up to five MP3/WAV/M4A/AAC/FLAC/OGG/WEBM samples (10 MB each, 25 MB total), name the voice, and the new voice_id appears with a copy button and in every voice dropdown in the app immediately; existing clones are listed with their description and a delete button. SPEECH TO SPEECH: upload a take, pick a target voice, keep the words, timing and emotion and swap only the timbre, with a remove-background-noise toggle and the same delivery sliders. DUBBING & TRANSLATION: upload a video/audio file (up to 50 MB, stored in workspace storage) or paste a public URL, pick a target language from a two-group list — ElevenLabs' documented 29 Core languages, then an Extended group (Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, Vietnamese, Hebrew, Hungarian, Norwegian) whose availability depends on the plan behind the key — set the source language (auto-detect by default) and speaker count (auto, or 1–5), toggle the free-tier watermark, then watch a four-row progress rail with a real elapsed-time progress bar while the job is polled every 5 seconds, and download the dubbed track when it lands. SOUND EFFECTS: a prompt box with Indian-context examples (busy Mumbai street, monsoon thunder on a tin roof, stadium roar, dhol intro hit), a 0.5–22s duration slider or model-chosen length, and a prompt-influence slider. AI MUSIC: describe a bed (Bollywood fusion, cinematic suspense, lo-fi, reel drop) with a length slider up to 5 minutes, an instrumental-only toggle and an engine toggle between ElevenLabs (exact length) and Google Lyria. AVATAR LIP-SYNC: the full ElevenLabs → HeyGen pipeline — script, voice, then a thumbnail grid of the account's live HeyGen avatars and talking photos with an Indian-only filter and per-card flag button, a 16:9 / 9:16 aspect toggle and a background colour picker; the voice is generated first, the audio is handed to HeyGen as a public URL, the render is polled every 4 seconds behind a four-step progress rail (Generating the voice → Handing the audio to HeyGen → Rendering → Done) and finishes as an inline player with Download MP4. ROUTING, which is the one thing to be precise about: speech, sound effects and dubbing run on the FOUNDER'S OWN ElevenLabs key through the workspace secrets proxy, and the key verdict is probed once and latched, with three distinct messages for 'no key stored', 'the key was rejected' and 'the key is not allow-listed for api.elevenlabs.io'. Voice cloning, the voice changer and music run on the AUDOS-MANAGED ElevenLabs endpoints and are billed to the workspace wallet, because all three need a multipart body carrying real file bytes and the secrets proxy's multipart mode carries text fields only. Text to Speech falls back from the founder's key to the managed endpoint automatically, so it keeps working either way and says which engine produced the audio. No ElevenLabs or HeyGen key ever reaches the browser bundle. Nothing is persisted to WorkspaceDB — generated audio and video live in the open tab, and the Indian-voice/avatar flags and clone descriptions are kept in the visitor's own browser.

apps.name: Video Provider Lab
apps.description: An owner-only developer test panel: one shared prompt, one shared image attachment, and every video model the platform exposes in a single selector - 25 runnable entries across all 6 installed video plugins - so the same brief can be put through each provider and read side by side. Nothing in the app holds an API key, an environment variable or a BYOK secret; every request goes to a same-origin Audos proxy path that adds the provider credential server-side and bills the workspace wallet, with X-Workspace-DB-Token as the only credential sent. THREE FILES: labModels.ts is the catalog (what exists, which plugin powers it, which parameters it takes, how long to poll - the Group A, Kling, Higgsfield and Runway rosters are derived from lib/videoEngines.ts so a model id still lives in exactly one place), labClient.ts is the network layer (one submit -> poll pair per plugin, hitting the proxies directly and deliberately NOT going through lib/videoEngineClient.ts, which would charge the customer credit ledger and can raise the plans screen), and App.tsx is only the panel. ENTRIES: image-and-video-generation + google-veo3 on POST /api/veo/generate/video -> GET /api/veo/status/:operationId for Seedance 2.0 Fast (ByteDance via OpenRouter), Gemini Omni Flash, Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.0, Veo 3.0 Fast, Veo 2.0, Sora 2, Sora 2 Pro and the OpenRouter Veo 3.1 / Fast / Lite variants, plus the platform-managed POST /api/generate/video which takes no model field; kling-video on POST /api/generate/kling/{text-to-video, image-to-video, multi-image} -> GET /api/generate/kling/status/:taskId for kling-v2-master, v1-6, v1-5 and v1, where the attached images pick the route (none = text-to-video, one = image-to-video, two to four = Elements) and a finished clip offers Extend +5s and TTS lip-sync; higgsfield-media on POST /api/generate/higgsfield/video (MiniMax Hailuo 02) and /image-to-video (DoP Turbo / Standard / Lite) -> GET /api/generate/higgsfield/status/:requestId, with moderation's nsfw status reported as its own outcome; heygen-video on POST .../heygen/proxy/v3/videos (avatar-led, the look and engine resolved from the live catalog, script capped at 500 characters) and .../v3/video-agents (prompt-driven, orientation rather than aspect ratio); runway-recipes on POST /api/generate/runway/quote first - free, unauthenticated, spends nothing - then /video with a fresh Idempotency-Key -> GET /api/generate/runway/status/:taskId for Gen 4.5 and Gen 4 Turbo, with the rest of the Runway roster listed but disabled until the capabilities endpoint lists it. Luma Dream Machine and Pika appear greyed out with the reason the platform has no route for either, rather than being offered as choices that would only answer 400. NOTHING SUBSTITUTES A MODEL: the old id ladder is gone, every id comes from the documented proxy enum, and a rejection is reported with its status, its path and the exact id that was sent. Per-entry parameter controls: duration, aspect ratio, resolution (4K only where it is honoured), generate-audio, negative prompt, Kling std/pro mode and camera preset, cfgScale, seed, HeyGen fit and voice speed, and a seed-frame-vs-reference-ingredient image role on Veo 3.1 and Omni Flash. A searchable grid grouped by provider plus a full dropdown, a compare checkbox that runs several models on the same brief at once, and a run log keeping the last 24 runs with a status badge, a live elapsed timer, the parameters that run actually sent, the exact request paths made, an inline player with an MP4 link, and the real error text - 402 reads as insufficient wallet balance, and a request the endpoint would refuse is recorded as Not sent with the reason instead of being submitted. Polling is a 5s setInterval cleared on completion, on Stop polling and on unmount, with per-entry caps from 4:00 on the fast Veo routes to 8:00 on HeyGen and Runway. Nothing is persisted - a session lives in the open tab. Dark panel scoped to these files only (#0a0a0a background, #111 cards, #D4920A accent) so the VidVerge shell theme is untouched. Files: apps/VideoProviderLab/App.tsx, apps/VideoProviderLab/labModels.ts, apps/VideoProviderLab/labClient.ts.

apps.name: MotionType
apps.description: MotionType is a kinetic typography studio. A line of text (1-120 characters), a style preset (Cinematic, Energetic, Minimal, Dramatic, Glitch, Elegant), a pace (Slow, Normal, Fast) and a colour theme (Cosmic, Monochrome, Fire, Ice, Gold) go to Claude Opus 5 through the workspace Anthropic proxy, which returns a structured animation plan: animation name, total duration, stage background, and a per-word list carrying delay, duration, entrance, exit, font size, weight, colour, letter spacing, text transform and an emphasis flag. The reply is treated as UNTRUSTED INPUT. Every CSS value is matched against an allow-list before it reaches a declaration, every number is clamped to sane bounds, and a plan whose word sequence is not the user's own text is rejected outright with an inline error and a Retry button rather than quietly replaced by a hardcoded animation; the raw reply is logged to the console for debugging and the workspace token never is. A valid plan is compiled into real CSS @keyframes and played on a 16:9 stage as individually positioned absolute spans, supporting all eight entrances (fadeUp, fadeIn, scaleIn, slideLeft, slideRight, glitch, typewriter, blur) and all four exits (fadeOut, scaleOut, slideUp, none). The entrance animation takes fill-mode both and the exit takes forwards, which is what stops a backwards exit fill from overriding the entrance for the whole sequence. Every selector is prefixed with the mounted stage's own scope class and every keyframe name carries the matching suffix, so generated CSS cannot leak into the dock, the agent panel or another app. Play/replay and a loop toggle run off the plan's own duration, so a loop restarts only after the exits have finished, and toggling loop mid-playback changes the next boundary without tearing down the running sequence. Copy CSS exports a standalone stylesheet (scene box, word classes, every required @keyframes rule, delays, durations, fill modes and the background) that works outside React with no workspace class dependencies, and shows a two-second CSS copied! toast only on a successful clipboard write. Record Preview redraws the same plan on an offscreen 1280x720 canvas at 30fps through a SECOND renderer that shares the layout, the sequence clock and the easing curves with the CSS preview, records it with MediaRecorder and downloads a .webm; it is a faithful reconstruction rather than a screen capture, and where canvas capture or MediaRecorder is unavailable the app says so inline and points at the browser's own screen recorder instead. prefers-reduced-motion holds the stage on its finished composition while Copy CSS and Record Preview still produce the full animation. Files: apps/MotionType/App.tsx, apps/MotionType/components/MotionControls.tsx, apps/MotionType/components/MotionStage.tsx, apps/MotionType/lib/motionPlan.ts, apps/MotionType/lib/motionLayout.ts, apps/MotionType/lib/motionCss.ts, apps/MotionType/lib/motionRecorder.ts.

apps.name: CineAgent
apps.description: CineAgent is the fully autonomous AI video EDITOR: upload raw footage (talking head, tutorial, screen recording, ad, podcast, vlog, interview — any type) and the agent owns the entire post-production: it analyzes, directs, edits, designs motion graphics, scores, renders, reviews its own cut and delivers a finished 1080p MP4 — no scene plans, prompts, model picking or settings required from the user (optional preferences exist but are never a prerequisite). PIPELINE: (1) upload to workspace storage with duration/aspect probing; (2) ANALYSIS — the audio track is decoded in-browser to 16kHz WAV for Deepgram nova-3 word-level transcription plus local silence detection, Gemini watches the complete video (including the ending) through /api/generate/video-analysis and returns structured scenes/key moments/on-screen text/quality notes, and ffmpeg frame extraction samples stills at scene boundaries + uniform coverage + the ending; (3) DIRECTION — Claude Opus 5 (via the workspace Anthropic proxy, with real frames attached as vision blocks) acts as editor/creative director/motion designer and authors a structured EditPlan: source cuts timed into transcript gaps, pacing, a content-matched visual identity, motion-graphic overlays chosen from a 14-primitive vocabulary (kinetic titles, lower thirds, callouts, animated stats/charts/timelines/lists, quotes, chapter cards, badges, keyword pops, image panels, progress arcs) PLUS a free-form keyframed 'custom' layer system so it can invent compositions — all as JSON, never as generated code; (4) ASSETS — generated video inserts run on Seedance 2.0 Fast / Veo 3.1 / Omni Flash through /api/veo/generate/video with a documented fallback ladder and optional source-frame seeding for continuity (never silently substituted — the registry records the engine that actually produced each clip), images on gemini-3.1-flash-image re-uploaded to durable GCS URLs, an ElevenLabs/Lyria underscore sized to the cut with speech-envelope ducking, optional ElevenLabs narration; (5) RENDER — ONE deterministic server-side Remotion pass (1920x1080/30fps) through /api/render/remotion: a hand-written runtime (apps/CineAgent/lib/motionRuntime.ts) interprets the plan — OffthreadVideo source segments with blurred-fill fit or cover framing, five transition types, every graphic primitive, burned captions baked deterministically from the word timestamps through the cut (clean/bold/karaoke/minimal/editorial presets), and mixed audio — so a render can never fail on director syntax; cuts past ~9.5 minutes render as chunks and concatenate via the ffmpeg stitch endpoint; (6) REVIEW — mechanical checks on the real file (playability, duration vs plan) then Opus vision reads frames of the FINISHED render against the plan and names defects; actionable defects trigger a targeted plan revision and re-render, capped at two passes, best-scoring cut ships with open notes documented honestly. Every stage checkpoints to the cine_projects WorkspaceDB table so a refresh resumes the run; asset and analysis work is never re-paid. UI is three states in one screen: a drop-zone home with optional creative preferences (tone note, captions/music/framing/motion intensity) and a resumable project grid; a run view with a seven-stage rail, live agent activity log and an optional 'see what the agent decided' plan inspector; and a result view with inline player, Download MP4, the reviewer's score and any open notes. Standalone — shares nothing with Video Enhancer or any other app. Files: apps/CineAgent/App.tsx + apps/CineAgent/lib/{types,ai,platform,audio,plan,director,assets,motionRuntime,render,qa,pipeline,store}.ts.

apps.name: Brand Context
apps.description: Brand Context is the paste-once brand primer: one screen that shows the workspace's full brand brief already formatted as a ChatGPT-ready prompt block — brand name, what Vidverge does, target audience, the core problem, the differentiator, the video format, the tone and the full credit pricing — so the customer never re-types brand details before asking an external AI for work. A read-only terminal-style block renders the text with a visible copy affordance in its title bar, a full-width Copy to Clipboard button puts it on the clipboard (Clipboard API first, hidden-textarea fallback where the browser blocks it) and confirms with a checkmark for two seconds before resetting, and three numbered hint cards close the loop: paste the block into a new ChatGPT conversation, ask for a 30-second script, then bring the script back into Script-to-Video or the Vidverge Agent. Entirely static and standalone — no AI calls, no WorkspaceDB, no auth; the copied text lives in the BRAND_CONTEXT constant in apps/BrandContext/App.tsx, which is the single place to edit the brand. Styled with the shared obsidian design system (components/ui/AppShell, Card, Button, Badge over components/theme tokens).
